title: Sanders amendment: Most Favored Nation drug pricing
question: On the Motion to Waive All Applicable Budgetary Discipline Re: Sanders Amdt. No. 5159 to S.Con.Res. 33 (budget resolution)
yes_means: Yes was a vote to let the Senate consider an amendment to cut U.S. prescription drug prices by more than half by capping them at the prices paid in Europe and Canada (Most Favored Nation pricing). It needed 60 votes and the vote tied 49-49.
industry_position: PhRMA, the drugmakers' trade group, lobbied members of Congress to resist legislation that would write Most Favored Nation drug pricing into law.

title: Add an extension of the expanded ACA premium tax credits to H.R. 1
question: On the Motion to Waive Section 302(f) of the Congressional Budget Act Re: S.Amdt. 2696 to H.R. 1
yes_means: Yes was a vote to let the Senate add an extension of the enhanced Affordable Care Act premium tax credits, paid for by a higher tax rate on income over $10 million, to the 2025 budget reconciliation bill. It needed 60 votes and got 47.
industry_position: AHIP, the health insurers' trade group, urged Congress to extend the enhanced premium tax credits before they expired at the end of 2025.

title: House gives final approval to H.R. 1
question: On Motion to Concur in the Senate Amendment to H.R. 1
yes_means: Yes was a vote to send the Senate-passed budget reconciliation bill, with its Medicaid work requirements, Medicaid financing limits and new marketplace enrollment rules, to the President to become law.
industry_position: After the Senate passed the bill, AHIP warned it could bring the biggest rollback in health coverage in U.S. history and urged Congress to change course.

title: Extend the expanded ACA premium tax credits
question: On the Cloture Motion to proceed to S. 3385
yes_means: Yes was a vote to move forward a bill extending for three years the enhanced premium tax credits that lower the cost of Affordable Care Act marketplace insurance. It needed 60 votes and got 51.
industry_position: AHIP urged Congress to extend the enhanced premium tax credits, paired with added program-integrity measures, for the 24 million people relying on them.

title: House passes a three-year extension of the expanded ACA premium tax credits
question: On Passage of H.R. 1834, the Breaking the Gridlock Act
yes_means: Yes was a vote to pass a bill extending the enhanced Affordable Care Act premium tax credits for three years. It reached the floor through a discharge petition and passed 230-196.
industry_position: AHIP urged Congress to extend the enhanced premium tax credits, paired with added program-integrity measures, for the 24 million people relying on them.

title: House passes H.R. 1, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act
question: On Passage of H.R. 1
yes_means: Yes was a vote to pass the House version of the 2025 budget reconciliation bill. Its health provisions included new Medicaid work requirements and limits on how states finance their share of Medicaid, including a freeze on provider taxes.
industry_position: The American Hospital Association urged the House to reject the bill's Medicaid and marketplace cuts, which it said would cut federal Medicaid support by more than $700 billion.

title: Kim amendment: strike H.R. 1's limits on Medicaid payments
question: On the Amendment S.Amdt. 2817 to H.R. 1
yes_means: Yes was a vote to remove the bill's limits on certain Medicaid payments to states and providers, which hospitals said would cut what Medicaid pays them.
industry_position: The American Hospital Association asked senators to change the bill's limits on state-directed payments and provider taxes, which it said went far beyond the House bill.

title: Senate passes H.R. 1, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act
question: On Passage of the Bill H.R. 1
yes_means: Yes was a vote to pass the 2025 budget reconciliation bill, which added Medicaid work requirements and limits on provider taxes and state-directed payments. It passed 50-50 with the Vice President breaking the tie.
industry_position: The American Hospital Association urged the Senate to reject the bill unless it was changed, warning its limits on provider taxes and state-directed payments would close hospitals, especially in rural areas.

title: House passes sanctions on the International Criminal Court
question: On Passage of H.R. 23, the Illegitimate Court Counteraction Act
yes_means: Yes was a vote to pass a bill imposing sanctions on people who help the International Criminal Court investigate or prosecute Americans or citizens of allied countries, including Israel.
industry_position: AIPAC supported the bill and commended the House for passing it.

title: Advance sanctions on the International Criminal Court
question: On Cloture on the Motion to Proceed to H.R. 23
yes_means: Yes was a vote to begin debate on the House-passed bill imposing sanctions on people who help the International Criminal Court investigate or prosecute Americans or citizens of allied countries, including Israel. It needed 60 votes and got 54.
industry_position: AIPAC supported H.R. 23 and commended the House for passing it before the Senate vote.

title: Sanders resolution: block an arms sale to Israel (April 2025)
question: On the Motion to Discharge S.J.Res. 33
yes_means: Yes was a vote to bring to the floor a resolution disapproving a proposed U.S. sale of defense articles and services to Israel. It failed 15-82.
industry_position: AIPAC urged its members to oppose the Sanders resolutions and praised the Senate for rejecting them.

title: Greene amendment: cut $500 million in Israel missile-defense funding
question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (Greene, Part A Amendment No. 114) to H.R. 4016, Defense Appropriations Act, 2026
yes_means: Yes was a vote to strike $500 million for U.S.-Israel cooperative missile-defense programs from the 2026 defense spending bill. It failed 6-422.
industry_position: AIPAC called the amendment reckless and welcomed its defeat.

title: Sanders resolution: block a sale of assault rifles to Israel
question: On the Motion to Discharge S.J.Res. 41
yes_means: Yes was a vote to bring to the floor a resolution disapproving a proposed export of defense articles to Israel, reported as tens of thousands of automatic assault rifles. It failed 27-70.
industry_position: AIPAC opposed the resolutions and praised the Senate for again rejecting Sanders' attempt to ban the weapons sales.

title: Sanders resolution: block a sale of bulldozers to Israel
question: On the Motion to Discharge S.J.Res. 32
yes_means: Yes was a vote to bring to the floor a resolution disapproving a proposed U.S. sale of defense articles to Israel, reported as military bulldozers. It failed 40-59.
industry_position: AIPAC called the resolutions misguided and dangerous and thanked the senators who voted against them.

title: Sanders resolution: block a sale of bombs to Israel
question: On the Motion to Discharge S.J.Res. 138
yes_means: Yes was a vote to bring to the floor a resolution disapproving a proposed U.S. sale of defense articles to Israel, reported as 1,000-pound bombs. It failed 36-63.
industry_position: AIPAC called the resolutions misguided and dangerous and thanked the senators who voted against them.
